# Why $NVDA fell after beating estimates

The drop was about expectations. The data I pulled don't show AI demand breaking.

**What the quarter delivered**
- Revenue was $30.0B [E5], up 122% from a year ago [E7].
- Data Center revenue was $26.3B [E5], up 154% [E5].
- Non-GAAP EPS was $0.68 [E2] against a $0.63 estimate [E2].

**Why the stock fell anyway**
- **Small beat.** The EPS beat was 7.94% [C4], the smallest in six quarters. In the July 2023 quarter it was 30.43% [C5].
- **No big raise.** Reuters called the forecast "largely in-line" for a stock used to beating by massive margins [E6].
- **Lower margins.** Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 75.7% [E7] from 78.9% [E7].
- **Blackwell delay.** Blackwell needed a mask change to improve yield, and its ramp starts in the fourth quarter [E7].

**The rest of the AI trade held up**
- $NVDA moved -6.38% [E12] on the day.
- $SMH moved -1.24% [E12] and $AMD moved -0.59% [E12].
- $SPY moved +0.01% [E12].

## Conclusion

Nvidia beat, but by its smallest margin in six quarters at 7.94% [C4]. Guidance was in line rather than a raise [E6], gross margin slipped to 75.7% [E7] and Blackwell needed a production fix [E7]. For a stock priced for repeated big surprises, that was enough for a -6.38% [E12] session. Peers barely moved, with $SMH at -1.24% [E12], and the market was flat, with $SPY at +0.01% [E12]. That points to an Nvidia-specific reset of expectations, not a collapse of the AI trade.

Whether selling fits you depends on your cost basis, horizon and concentration. Your portfolio isn't loaded here, so I can't see those. The fundamental test ahead is whether Blackwell delivers "several billion dollars" of revenue in the fourth quarter as guided [E7].

**What I couldn't confirm:**
- I couldn't retrieve the exact Q3 guide or the revenue consensus.
- Two report figures are unverified: the index reference in the Reaction text and the margin-decline wording in the Stance.

*This is research, not investment advice.*

The catch is that the yield isn't income in the usual sense, and it isn't reliable. The funds also have annual expenses of 1.01% [E6], and their payouts depend on one volatile stock.

The open question is total return: price change plus all distributions since launch. I didn't have the distribution history, so I couldn't compute it.

*This is research, not investment advice.*

- Debt of about $7.21B [C9] equals 20.03% of the value of its Bitcoin [C10].

- The newest notes pay 0% interest and mature in 2029 [E4], so a Bitcoin price drop does not trigger a margin call.
